2.1. INTRODUCTION
This Risk Management Program is designed to comply with the Environmental Protection Agency regulations detailed in 40 CFR Part 68. The stationary source is the ammonia refrigeration system owned and operated by Associated Wholesale Grocers, 8100 60th Street, Kenosha, WI 53144-7863. The only RMP regulated substance at this facility is anhydrous ammonia. It is classified as a highly hazardous chemical, liquefied under pressure.
This is an existing food distribution facility acquired by AWG in 2016. There is one ammonia refrigeration system at this facility with an inventory of 28260 pounds of ammonia. The process does not meet the requirements of Program 1. It is subject to OSHAs PSM standard. Therefore, this RMP is written to meet compliance for a RMP/PSM Level 3 prevention program.
This facility has an excellent safety record with no deaths or serious injuries to plant personnel or contractors due to the RMP covered process. The system was commissioned in Jan 2009 under a previous owner and there have been no accidents in the following years of system operation. No Ammonia has ever been added to this system due to accidental release in the years of operation. The facility's safety record is a direct result of the emphasis placed on safety by management and employees alike.

2.2. ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION POLICIES AND PROGRAM
This facility strives to meet or exceed compliance with state anhydrous ammonia regulations. The company's Environmental, Health & Safety staff provides technical assistance and performs safety and environmental audits on a regular basis. Training is provided for each new hire and rehire employee and on a monthly basis through an interactive safety program named Alchemy. In addition to safety training, designated employees are certified in First Aid and CPR.
The anhydrous ammonia system and associated equipment are inspected annually by the state of Wisconsin and a Permit to Operate is issued and kept on display in the en

gine room. Additionally, AWG inspects the system annually following recommended industry and engineering frequencies.

2.3. EMERGENCY POLICIES AND PROGRAM
Each employee is trained to be familiar with the emergency policies and procedures through safety reviews and other safety meetings. This facility has an Emergency Action Plan (EAP) which covers accidental releases, natural disasters, security incidents and other emergency practices and procedures. The Emergency Action Plan for this facility is reviewed and updated on an annual basis as part of a comprehensive review process. The Emergency Action Plan for this facility includes specific instructions for employees regarding the procedures for each type of emergency. The procedures may differ by circumstance depending on the emergency, qualifications of the personnel and equipment available onsite.
The procedures provided in the Emergency Action Plan are shared with all employees and followed in the event of an emergency. Employees are provided with refresher training on what to do in an emergency on an annual basis and drills are performed, documented, and evaluated for improvements.
The local emergency planning committee and fire department personnel have been provided with a copy of the Emergency Action Plan (EAP) for this facility and invited for a tour on an annual basis. This plan is available to the local Fire Department and LEPC.

2.4. WORST-CASE SCENARIO/ALTERNATIVE-CASE SCENARIO
This facility has developed a worst-case and alternative-case scenario however it has been withheld from this Executive Summary for security-sensitive information as requested by EPA.

2.5. FIVE YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY
This facility has an excellent safety record with no deaths or serious injuries to any of its personnel or contractors as a result of the RMP covered process. In addition, there have been no accidents resulting in releases of anhydrous ammonia with off-site consequences during the entire operation period. Extensive pro

grams and procedures are in place to maintain this record.

2.6. PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY
Associated Wholesale Grocers continuously look for ways to enhance the safety of this location. Inspections to equipment are conducted and appropriate follow-ups made based on the equipment manufacturers guidelines. Rounds and Inspection details are available in the Engine Room Office. Detailed Compliance Audits are conducted every three years  recommendations and follow up are available in the Engine Room Office or the office of the EHS. Emergency drills for weather, fire and chemical release are conducted annually and documented. A procedure is established to meet, evaluate, and follow up on improvements noted.

2.7. SUMMARY
The employees of Associated Wholesale Grocers are proud of our safety record and our continual improvement program. We believe with our programs and policies in place and with the continued efforts of our personnel, we will maintain our safety record and our safe facility environment for the public, our customers, and our employees for years to come.
